content:
Andrew: Quick ask — planning a quick sweep of max_batch_tokens for continuous batching tonight. Can someone run a mini throughput sweep on staging (10m runs) for token sizes [512, 1024, 2048, 4096]? Need p50/p95/p99 and toks/sec. Prefer results before EOD. ping @Maya @Jing
Maya: I can take 512/1024. Which model variant — redwood-v1 or redwood-lite? And which queue_policy (default/latency)?
Andrew: redwood-v1-8k (fp16 quant). queue_policy=latency. Use cb-config `cb_sweep_2026.yaml` in my PR #842 (links in PR).
Maya: grabbing the PR. I'll kick off: `./tools/run_bench --model redwood-v1 --config cb_sweep_2026.yaml --tokens 512,1024 --duration 10m --tag maya-mini`
ci-bot: Started bench job maya-mini-1890022337 on staging-node-3. Link: https://ci.example/bench/1890022337
Leo: I'll take 2048/4096 later tonight — heads up that the cluster autoscaler might spin up a node and affect steady-state. I'll set `max_batch_wait_ms=8` for low latency runs.
Jing: Quick question — do we want KV-cache warmup included? Warmup tends to change steady-state behavior.
Andrew: yes, include a warmup (200 requests). Add `--warmup 2m`. That should bring the KV cache up.
Sam: FYI I saw a p99 spike on a prior 4096 run; suspect GPU memcpy during fallback paths. If it shows up again, add profiling: `--profile gpu memcpy` so we can capture traces.
Maya: 512/1024 runs finished — results pasted below. No obvious regressions for these configs.
```
# maya-mini results (staging-node-3) tag=maya-mini
tokens p50_ms p95_ms p99_ms toks_per_sec
512    12       34      48     21000
1024   18       60      120    17000
warmup: ok
notes: steady-state after ~90s
```
Maya: CI artifacts uploaded: https://ci.example/bench/1890022337/artifacts. Updated PR with the metrics link + short blurb.
ci-bot: Job maya-mini-1890022337 completed. Artifacts: https://ci.example/bench/1890022337/artifacts
Leo: starting 2048/4096 now. For 4096 I'll enable `--profile gpu` and capture nvprof traces.
Leo: 2048 done — quick paste: 
```
# leo-run-2048
tokens p50_ms p95_ms p99_ms toks_per_sec
2048   30      95     210    12000
```
Leo: 4096 first try hung at ~6m (queue backlog spike). Retried with a slightly higher `max_batch_tokens=6000` fallback and that finished but p99=420ms (higher than acceptable). Uploading logs: https://ci.example/bench/1890022337/leo-4096
Jing: Can you attach the trace/span for the marshal/serialize stage? If memcpy is the culprit, it shows up there. Also which allocator (cudaMalloc vs caching) in that run?
Leo: trace & logs uploaded. Allocator: caching allocator (default). Link: https://ci.example/bench/1890022337/leo-4096/traces
Carol: quick ops question — if 4096 is flaky, are we comfortable advertising 4k max_batch_tokens for Dedicated customers? I'd prefer a canary (25% traffic) first.
Andrew: +1 to canary. Let's hold on broad rollout until we confirm stability. If 4096 consistently spikes, default should be 2048.
Sam: I'll add a small CI perf regression test that exercises 4096 with a mocked memcpy path so we catch regressions early. Will open PR.
Maya: one more datapoint — latency distribution plot in the notebook: https://notebooks.example/plots/1890022337 (:chart_with_upwards_trend:)
Andrew: thanks. Action items: (1) Leo to try one more 4096 run with `--cuda-allocator=caching --max_batch_wait_ms=6` and full `--profile gpu memcpy`. (2) Sam to open CI perf test PR. (3) Carol to draft canary rollout plan at 25% traffic for Dedicated. (4) I will collate results and update the rollout doc and PR description; tag me when done.
Leo: running final 4096 attempt now, will post results.
ci-bot: Reminder: nightly sweep scheduled at 02:00 UTC. If you want a different window, reply here.
Leo: final 4096 attempt completed. Summary: second try still elevated p99=390ms, memcpy hotspots in trace at t=~3.2s. Attaching flamegraph.
```
# leo-run-4096-final
tokens p50_ms p95_ms p99_ms toks_per_sec
4096   110     260    390    9000
notes: memcpy hotspot in model->output copy at ~3.2s
```
Jing: Thanks — that lines up with the previous hypothesis. I'll prep a small patch to reduce copies in the output path (low-risk change). Will open PR and tag runtime for review.
Andrew: great. Once Jing's patch lands, let's rerun the 4096 sweep overnight. If p99 drops under 300ms we can consider a cautious canary.
Maya: bookmarking results and closing out my runs. Ping me if you want me to re-run 512/1024 with the new allocator flags.
Carol: drafting canary doc now — will share ETA in #eng-release.
Sam: PR for CI perf test created: https://git.example/r/perf-tests/pull/107. Adds a synthetic memcpy check during 4096 runs.
Andrew: Thanks all. I'll assemble a short summary and update the PR + rollout doc. If anyone hits anything odd overnight, reply here and I'll triage in the morning.
Maya: on it.
ci-bot: Nightly sweep scheduled & completed jobs will be archived in 72h.
